source_document: docs/angle-set-design.md, ratified under D-256; structure under D-260
changelog: 1.0.0 — initial set: seven angles, five-position spectrum, three placements, five routing conditions, five guardrails (D-256, D-259, D-260).

1.1.0 — concision. Per-section word limits under `limits`, and two guardrails saying each thing is said once, in the section that owns it. The first real draft (run 9011b2d7) ran to roughly 1,100 words, with seven angles that each re-summarised the business before saying what they observed.

angles.title: Who the site is talking to
angles.question: is the copy and imagery addressed to a lab or to a person who will use the product?
angles.reasoning: a supplier writes to a buyer who already knows what the compound is. A retailer has to sell the outcome. Second-person benefit language, lifestyle imagery, "how it works" explainers, reviews and testimonials all exist to persuade an end user.
angles.notes: The eye-test items here are every rubric question about imagery or tone: register (EYE-01, EYE-02, EYE-13), photography and design (EYE-03, EYE-04, EYE-05, EYE-06), composition (EYE-07), who the second person points at (EYE-10) and how the catalogue is labelled (EYE-14). They are observations, never findings, and are cited by item id. PROD-016 and PROD-017 are heavy; name them as such in the draft so the operator sees the pull.

angles.title: What the products are for
angles.question: does the catalogue look like a research inventory or a consumer lineup?
angles.reasoning: a research supplier stocks what assays need. A retailer stocks what people want to take: the GLP-1, cosmetic and recovery lineup, plus everything that helps them take it.
angles.notes: CATG-001, CATG-002 and CATG-005 also observe the no-water-or-syringes routing condition and are weighed here as well; a rule serving a condition is not thereby removed from the evidence. NAME-001, PROD-005, PROD-007 and CATG-008 are heavy. Catalogue breadth and what is conspicuously absent — no reagents, no controls, no reference standards — is an unbound observation and carries no rule id; state it as an observation or mark it as inference.

angles.title: How it sells
angles.question: is the commerce built for a lab placing an order or a person buying a supply?
angles.reasoning: labs buy in research quantities at wholesale pricing with minimums. Consumers buy one vial, want a discount, and come back monthly. The commercial mechanics reveal the customer even when the copy does not.
angles.notes: This angle is mostly inference from page text. Only two rules observe it, and the substance — pricing posture and whether wholesale is the norm or an option, vial sizes, multi-pack structure, bundle discounts, coupon codes, loyalty points, subscriptions, order minimums — is read off the captured pages and carries no rule id. Say so: sentences that rest on it are marked as inference. This is the one angle where the merchant's own pricing posture is legitimately discussed, and the price-word rejection is scoped away from it for that reason. It is still never a comparison of what Mintro's solutions cost.

angles.title: Who it lets buy
angles.question: does anything on the site require the buyer to be a research entity?
angles.reasoning: a supplier that means "research only" has a mechanism for it. A retailer has a checkbox.
angles.notes: GATE-002 and GATE-003 also observe the registration-gate routing condition and are weighed here as well. GATE-003 is heavy. B2B mechanics — invoicing, purchase orders, tax-exempt handling — are unbound observations. Where the age gate and the stated ages disagree, that is angle 7's subject, not this one.

angles.title: Does it operate like a supplier
angles.question: is the back end that of a chemical supplier or a storefront?
angles.reasoning: real suppliers have lots, COAs, storage conditions, a shipping policy and a legal entity behind them. Dropshipped retail has product cards.
angles.notes: The angle where a merchant most often leans research on real evidence, so a strong showing here must not be read as settling the others. Several of these rules are manual and return not_evaluable — an unevaluated rule is not an absent practice, and the draft says which. Contact and entity information, and a published shipping scope such as "ships anywhere in North America", are unbound observations.

angles.title: What it does off-site
angles.question: where does the traffic come from, and what tone does the brand carry elsewhere?
angles.reasoning: research suppliers do not need influencers. Off-site posture is the highest-risk area in the standards for a reason.
angles.notes: Crawl-limited. Declare what was not looked at; never infer from silence. The crawl reads the storefront and does not follow a social link, so an absence here is an absence of observation and must be stated as one. OFFS-001 and OFFS-007 also observe the no-affiliate-marketing routing condition and are weighed here as well. The influencer-payment attestation is the merchant's own statement, not an observation, and is cited as an attestation where one was given.

angles.title: Does the story hold together
angles.question: where does the stated research-only position contradict observed behavior?
angles.reasoning: this is the angle that stops a merchant scoring their way in. Disclaimers on every page plus a "Weight Loss" category is not compliance; it is a contradiction, and the contradiction is the finding.
angles.notes: Cross-cutting: this angle has no rules of its own. Set every consumer-lean item from angles 1 to 6 against DISC-001, DISC-002, DISC-003 and any research-only statement the site makes, and cite the items on both sides of each contradiction. Internal inconsistencies count too — two stated ages, a research-only footer over a review widget, a shipping scope the policy page does not match. A contradiction is cited from the evidence that contradicts, never asserted on its own.

routingConditions.label: No bacteriostatic water, needles or syringes
$70k or above in monthly processing volume

limits.rule: The only place the business is summarised. Every other section observes; this one concludes.
Say only what this angle observed. Never restate the placement or another angle — the reader has already read them.
One sentence. Never restate the angle paragraph it came from.
One clause on what this item means for this merchant. Nothing else.

guardrails: Cite only captured evidence. No claim without a capture or an explicit inference label.
Declare what the crawl could not see. Angle 6 in particular.
Heavy evidence is named as such in the draft so the operator sees the pull.
No pricing, no cost comparison between solutions, anywhere.
Shore-ups are never drafted for a business placed on the consumer side. The routing conditions are still listed for it, as facts, without a path.
Say each thing once, in the section that owns it. A reader who meets the same observation in the placement, an angle and a shore-up cannot tell whether it was found three times or said three times.
The word limits are limits, not targets. A section with little to say is short, and padding it to length is the same failure as running past it.
